sections.narration: Christopher F. Foss, “S-400,” in Jane’s Land Warfare Platforms: Artillery and Air Defense, (London: IHS Global, 2016), 577.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Russia’s S-400 surface to air missile system and its Su-35 fighters in Syria are a major headache for the US-led coalition.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: In November 2015, a Turkish F-16 shot down a Russian Air Force Su-24 Fencer bomber for violating Turkish airspace on the border with Syria.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: In response, Russia pointedly deployed its most capable operational air defence system, the S-400 Triumf, to Latakia air base.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Analysis and reactions at the time focussed on the formidable theoretical capabilities of the S-400 and its huge advertised 400 km range which would place a large portion of Syria, the eastern Mediterranean and southern Turkey inside its missile engagement zone.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Russia also bases four of its most modern operational air superiority fighter, the Sukhoi Su-35S, in Syria.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: The Su-35 is the next step in the evolution of the famous Su-27/30 Flanker family of 1980s vintage, and can theoretically pose a serious danger to all coalition aircraft with the exception of the scarce and extremely expensive US Air Force F-22 Raptor stealth fighter.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: The S-400 surface to air missile (SAM) system is one of Russia’s most important assets in Syria, as well as in Eastern Europe where the system’s presence in the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad gives the Kremlin powerful airspace denial options over the Baltic States and much of Poland.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: The S-400 system consists of wheeled vehicles including long-range surveillance radars, tracking and engagement radars, missile transportation and launch vehicles, and a command and control node.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: In practice, the system’s engagement range is far shorter than the advertised 400 km since the very long-range 40N6 missile is still in testing and non-operational, limiting the system to engagements inside 250 km.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: However, the S-400 is rightly considered one of the most capable SAM systems in service anywhere in the world and is one of the most feared threats that a Western fighter pilot could encounter in combat today.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Even if attacked, the S-400 battery at Latakia is protected by the Pantsir S-1 point defence system which combines radar guided rapid-firing cannons and short range missiles to intercept incoming threats at short range including precision guided munitions.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: On paper, therefore, the S-400 gives Russia the ability to threaten or even halt US-led coalition air operations over most of Syria.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: The largely ineffectual strike by US Navy ships using 60 BGM-109 Tomahawk land attack cruise missiles (TLAMs) against the Syrian Air Force base at Shayrat – in response to a chemical weapons attack on Khan Sheikhoun two days previously – was the first major illustration of Russia’s difficulties surrounding its air defence capabilities in Syria.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: In the days following the US strike, many questioned why Russia's much vaunted S-400 had not been used to intercept the US TLAMs during their subsonic flight towards Shayrat, despite Russia having been given sufficient advanced warning by the US military to evacuate any personnel or equipment that they had on the base.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: The S-400 battery at Latakia can fire between 36 and 48 missiles (depending on whether medium or heavy launcher vehicles are used) before needing to reload.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Therefore, had Russia attempted to engage the TLAMs with the S-400 system, it would not have been able to destroy more than about half of the incoming missiles even assuming all of the SAMs loaded and ready were fired and all hit their intended single targets – an unlikely outcome.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: If – as is much more likely – some of the S-400 interceptor missiles had missed or malfunctioned (the system is still maturing and is not combat proven), then Russia’s key asset would have been shown to be far less effective even against fairly easy targets than the hype around its deployments in Syria and Kaliningrad assumed.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: This is probably the key reason why the S-400 system was not used to defend Shayrat – a major military hub for Russia’s key ally.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: The shooting down of a Syrian Air Force Su-22 bomber by a US Navy F/A-18E Super Hornet on 18 June 2017 means – in effect – that the US is now calling the Russian air defence bluff in a much more open way.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Following the Turkish Su-24 shootdown and the US strike on Shayrat, Russia made threats and implied that it could target coalition aircraft to protect both its own assets and those of its Syrian ally.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Similarly, in June 2017 Russia threatened to track, ‘escort’ and treat coalition aircraft west of the Euphrates as targets using the S-400 and its own Su-35s.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: However, while each individual coalition sortie within range of the system using non-stealth aircraft would indeed be at very high risk if actually launched upon by the S-400, the Kremlin has compelling reasons to avoid doing so at all costs.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Moreover, if the S-400 were used, tit-for-tat escalation would very likely occur, and the Shayrat example shows how attacks with TLAMs and other standoff weapons could quickly overwhelm the S-400 and even its Pantsir point defences at Latakia.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Likewise Russia’s Su-35s and other Flanker derivatives in Syria are all capable of meeting coalition fighters other than the F-22 on equal terms one on one, but they are heavily outnumbered and would be very unlikely to come off better from a flashpoint engagement.

evidence.qualification: Reported by the cited source; not independently verified by this script.

sections.narration: Non-Western states which traditionally look to Russia have seen Turkey shoot down a Russian jet, with no lasting consequences, the US strike Shayrat air base with impunity and most recently shoot down a Syrian Air Force Su-22 (and two armed drones) within Russia’s vaunted air defence coverage again without notable consequences beyond angry rhetoric.

[
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-05608baa58e4c016",
    "text": "The S-400 Triumf (NATO: SA-21 Growler) is a mobile, surface-to-air missile system (SAM) designed by Russia.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",

  {
    "claim_id": "claim-c864a152f8aabe45",
    "text": "It represents the fourth generation of long-range Russian SAMs, and the successor to the S-200 and S-300.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",

    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-bbe4a04a2ff55af3",
    "text": "The S-400’s mission set and capabilities are roughly comparable to the U.S. Patriot system.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-8e2d3cb6f2fa1508",
    "text": "Unlike some Patriot interceptors today, however, the S-400 does not currently employ hit-to-kill ballistic missile defense technology.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-4f9f857108d6aef3",
    "text": "Russia began developing the S-400 in 1993.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-ddac8527c07fb5be",
    "text": "Between 70-80% of the technology employed by the initial S-400 design was taken and adapted from the S-300, including missile storage containers, launchers, and radars.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-5122b95464072cb3",
    "text": "The S-400 launchers were also designed to be compatible with S-300 interceptor variants.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-4d23366bfcfc6478",
    "text": "The first S-400 systems became operational in 2007 and entered service with the First Air Defense Corps responsible for defending Moscow.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-dbb04f96ebc7327f",
    "text": "The S-400 primarily uses the 48N6 missile series.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-f678719263224a04",
    "text": "Unlike other Russian SAMs, the 77N6 missiles will use hit-to-kill technology (as do PAC-3 missiles) and are designed specifically to destroy ballistic missile warheads.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-dc195dc4ccd2718d",
    "text": "The final missile series used by the S-400 is the 40N6, a long range family that can extend the air defense capabilities of the system to 400 km.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-43d358419430911f",
    "text": "6 The current deployment status of the 40N6 missile is unclear, and questions remain as to whether the S-400’s radar capabilities would allow the 40N6 make full use of its maximum range.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-1b65c74ed252afd6",
    "text": "Since entering service, the S-400 has seen several high-profile deployments, augmenting S-300s already operational in several key areas.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-581f5b8e8dce36fa",
    "text": "Notably, S-400 units are currently stationed in the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, where it defends Russia’s significant military presence from aerial attack.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-038c99fc90bac09c",
    "text": "Russia has also stationed S-400 units in Crimea to strengthen Russia’s position on the recently-annexed peninsula.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-201aa0005add79e8",
    "text": "In addition to being deployed by Russian forces, the S-400 has also been exported to other countries.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-bd29eaf90b44f3f1",
    "text": "See a visualization of Russian S-400 deployments on the interactive map, The Russia-NATO A2AD Environment.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-4274f70bba96fa4e",
    "text": "Christopher F. Foss, “S-400,” in Jane’s Land Warfare Platforms: Artillery and Air Defense, (London: IHS Global, 2016), 577.",
    "source_id": "148827db7320d204c6c3f4e53296339538cf636f",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-7bda0b745573d6fe",
    "text": "Russia’s S-400 surface to air missile system and its Su-35 fighters in Syria are a major headache for the US-led coalition.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-edf42a724a265a38",
    "text": "In November 2015, a Turkish F-16 shot down a Russian Air Force Su-24 Fencer bomber for violating Turkish airspace on the border with Syria.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-7eccfe56f6bf3267",
    "text": "In response, Russia pointedly deployed its most capable operational air defence system, the S-400 Triumf, to Latakia air base.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-40026d63f0b48516",
    "text": "Analysis and reactions at the time focussed on the formidable theoretical capabilities of the S-400 and its huge advertised 400 km range which would place a large portion of Syria, the eastern Mediterranean and southern Turkey inside its missile engagement zone.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-d14db917ace3f741",
    "text": "Russia also bases four of its most modern operational air superiority fighter, the Sukhoi Su-35S, in Syria.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-f90b9d820c9e78df",
    "text": "The Su-35 is the next step in the evolution of the famous Su-27/30 Flanker family of 1980s vintage, and can theoretically pose a serious danger to all coalition aircraft with the exception of the scarce and extremely expensive US Air Force F-22 Raptor stealth fighter.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-c9ad3f2dfd0e9fdb",
    "text": "The S-400 surface to air missile (SAM) system is one of Russia’s most important assets in Syria, as well as in Eastern Europe where the system’s presence in the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad gives the Kremlin powerful airspace denial options over the Baltic States and much of Poland.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-070207468492fc92",
    "text": "The S-400 system consists of wheeled vehicles including long-range surveillance radars, tracking and engagement radars, missile transportation and launch vehicles, and a command and control node.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-65e68724ed58635d",
    "text": "In practice, the system’s engagement range is far shorter than the advertised 400 km since the very long-range 40N6 missile is still in testing and non-operational, limiting the system to engagements inside 250 km.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-ce9d576bbee46bf8",
    "text": "However, the S-400 is rightly considered one of the most capable SAM systems in service anywhere in the world and is one of the most feared threats that a Western fighter pilot could encounter in combat today.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-39cb2023f171ce2e",
    "text": "Even if attacked, the S-400 battery at Latakia is protected by the Pantsir S-1 point defence system which combines radar guided rapid-firing cannons and short range missiles to intercept incoming threats at short range including precision guided munitions.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-934571cf2bbf0428",
    "text": "On paper, therefore, the S-400 gives Russia the ability to threaten or even halt US-led coalition air operations over most of Syria.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-81b9374744cdb649",
    "text": "The largely ineffectual strike by US Navy ships using 60 BGM-109 Tomahawk land attack cruise missiles (TLAMs) against the Syrian Air Force base at Shayrat – in response to a chemical weapons attack on Khan Sheikhoun two days previously – was the first major illustration of Russia’s difficulties surrounding its air defence capabilities in Syria.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-1a7fae4d33f5d6f7",
    "text": "In the days following the US strike, many questioned why Russia's much vaunted S-400 had not been used to intercept the US TLAMs during their subsonic flight towards Shayrat, despite Russia having been given sufficient advanced warning by the US military to evacuate any personnel or equipment that they had on the base.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-04fbaec460080873",
    "text": "The S-400 battery at Latakia can fire between 36 and 48 missiles (depending on whether medium or heavy launcher vehicles are used) before needing to reload.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-e9dda419329a0c6b",
    "text": "Therefore, had Russia attempted to engage the TLAMs with the S-400 system, it would not have been able to destroy more than about half of the incoming missiles even assuming all of the SAMs loaded and ready were fired and all hit their intended single targets – an unlikely outcome.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-c4150212d9250a64",
    "text": "If – as is much more likely – some of the S-400 interceptor missiles had missed or malfunctioned (the system is still maturing and is not combat proven), then Russia’s key asset would have been shown to be far less effective even against fairly easy targets than the hype around its deployments in Syria and Kaliningrad assumed.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-55a6fe6d596e7af0",
    "text": "This is probably the key reason why the S-400 system was not used to defend Shayrat – a major military hub for Russia’s key ally.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-f4352d14e39d8048",
    "text": "The shooting down of a Syrian Air Force Su-22 bomber by a US Navy F/A-18E Super Hornet on 18 June 2017 means – in effect – that the US is now calling the Russian air defence bluff in a much more open way.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-7e4cf1ea148747cb",
    "text": "Following the Turkish Su-24 shootdown and the US strike on Shayrat, Russia made threats and implied that it could target coalition aircraft to protect both its own assets and those of its Syrian ally.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-f39ecd8ff50b8267",
    "text": "Similarly, in June 2017 Russia threatened to track, ‘escort’ and treat coalition aircraft west of the Euphrates as targets using the S-400 and its own Su-35s.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
    "claim_id": "claim-ad51a92c1768a5d0",
    "text": "However, while each individual coalition sortie within range of the system using non-stealth aircraft would indeed be at very high risk if actually launched upon by the S-400, the Kremlin has compelling reasons to avoid doing so at all costs.",
    "source_id": "9310b0a55b625410bad0c205edc3a8cf18273981",
    "independent_sources": 1,
    "verified_fact_allowed": false,
    "allowed_statement_kinds": [
      "ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM",
      "ANALYSIS"
    ]
  },
  {
